lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the modern Rivina/Petiveriaceae split by emphasizing the single-carpel ovary and one-seeded berry.

project_scope.note: POWO/APG IV accepts Petiveriaceae and places Rivina here. Older floras often described Rivina under broad Phytolaccaceae.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: For the project genus Rivina, inspect the slender raceme of tiny 4-sepal flowers and then the bright red berry. The ovary is formed from a single carpel.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Herb or subshrub in the project genus; leaves simple, petiolate and alternate.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Rivina flowers are small, regular, usually 4-sepaled and 4-stamened, arranged in terminal or lateral racemes. Petals are absent.
family_diagnostics.fruit: A small globose fleshy red berry derived from one carpel and containing a single seed.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Pigeonberry looks pokeweed-ish at a glance, but the tiny red one-seeded berry and single-carpel plan put it in Petiveriaceae.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: slender raceme → 4-sepal flower → single carpel → red one-seeded berry → pokeweed comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Petiveriaceae is the perfect modern-taxonomy comparison family: it resembles pokeweed, but its reproductive plan is much simpler.

steps.title: 1 · Find the slender Rivina raceme
steps.look_for: Tiny pale flowers and red fruits distributed along a thin raceme.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the characteristic local whole-plant presentation.

steps.title: 2 · Zoom into the 4-part flower
steps.look_for: Four sepals and four stamens, with no separate petals.

steps.title: 3 · Follow one carpel into one red berry
steps.look_for: A small globose red berry containing a single seed.
steps.why_it_matters: The one-carpel plan is the cleanest split from Phytolacca.

comparisons.title: Petiveriaceae vs Phytolaccaceae
comparisons.rule: Rivina: one carpel → small one-seeded red berry. Phytolacca: several carpels → larger multi-lobed/multi-seeded berry.

comparisons.title: Petiveriaceae vs Nyctaginaceae
comparisons.rule: Rivina has tiny 4-sepal raceme flowers and a fleshy berry; Nyctaginaceae has a petaloid perianth and anthocarp.

visual_lesson.caveat: Older flora descriptions may still label Rivina as Phytolaccaceae. The project follows current POWO/APG family placement.

genera.fast_cue: thin raceme + tiny 4-part flowers + bright red one-seeded berries

visual_targets.structure: Rivina flower and berry on same raceme
